subject: Chemistry
description: Common gases, gas laws, Avogadro, STP conditions

questions.stem: The gas that makes up approximately 78% of the Earth's atmosphere is:
questions.explanation: Dry atmosphere composition: N₂ ~78%, O₂ ~21%, Ar ~0.93%, CO₂ ~0.04%. Water vapour varies. Biological N-fixation and industrial Haber-Bosch process both transform this abundant but inert N₂ into usable forms.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: A gas used to preserve food by INHIBITING OXIDATION in packaged snacks is:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen flushing — N₂ is inert, displaces O₂, prevents rancidity of oils and microbial growth. Used in chip packets, coffee bags, wine barrels. Same reason: nitrogen is used in IV-fluid bags and electronics packaging.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: BOYLE'S LAW states that at constant temperature, for a fixed mass of gas, pressure and volume are:
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: P ∝ 1/V → PV = constant (at constant T, n). Squeeze a syringe → volume halves, pressure doubles. Charles's law: V ∝ T at constant P. Combined: PV/T = constant → PV = nRT (ideal gas law).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which of the following is the LIGHTEST gas known?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen (molar mass ≈ 2 g/mol) is the lightest gas. Helium ≈ 4 g/mol is the lightest noble gas and is used in airships and balloons instead of H₂ because He is non-flammable (Hindenburg disaster made H₂ unsafe for passenger airships).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: At STP (Standard Temperature and Pressure: 0 °C, 1 atm), one mole of ANY ideal gas occupies a volume of:
questions.explanation: Avogadro's law → molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres. From PV = nRT with P = 1 atm, T = 273.15 K, n = 1, V = RT/P = (0.0821 × 273.15) ≈ 22.4 L. (Under the newer IUPAC STP with P = 100 kPa instead of 101.325 kPa, molar volume is 22.7 L — exam usually expects 22.4 L.)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The gas responsible for the DISTINCT SMELL OF ROTTEN EGGS and given off when hydrogen and sulphur combine is:
questions.explanation: Hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) — characteristic smell of rotten eggs. Toxic in higher concentrations (deadens olfactory nerves, so high doses are undetectable by smell). SO₂ has a choking sulphurous smell; NH₃ is pungent ammonia; CO is odourless and lethal.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The NOBLE GASES (Group 18) are generally unreactive because:

options.option_text: They have an incomplete outer shell
They have a complete outer electron shell (duet/octet)

questions.explanation: Helium has 2 outer electrons (duet); Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn have 8 (octet). Stable configuration → low reactivity. Xenon can form XeF₂, XeF₄, XeO₃ under strong oxidising conditions — so 'noble' not 'inert'. Argon is used in bulbs (displaces O₂). Neon — signs. Helium — MRI cooling.
